sentences.text: Patients with sickle cell disease (SCD) presenting to the emergency department and hematology clinic with temperature greater than or equal to 38 degrees C were prospectively evaluated using a physician-completed questionnaire.
Seventy-three patients with SCD with 96 febrile events were evaluated over a 1-year period.
The questionnaire was completed before obtaining chest radiography (CXR) results in all patients.
Twenty-four percent (23/96) of the patients had CXR evidence of acute chest syndrome (ACS).
On the basis of the questionnaire data, 61% (14/23) of ACS cases were not clinically suspected by the evaluating physician before obtaining CXR.

Comparing the patients with and without ACS revealed that, with the exception of splinting (4/23 [17%] versus 0/73 [0%]), no symptom or physical examination finding helped to identify which patients had ACS.
Fifty-seven percent of patients with ACS had completely normal findings on physical examination.
The presentation of patients with clinically detected versus clinically unsuspected ACS also did not differ significantly.
Overall physician sensitivity for predicting ACS was only 39%, and diagnostic accuracy did not improve significantly with increasing levels of pediatric training.

The evidence on whether a dedicated discharge coordinator improves the quality of hospital discharge is mixed: in an intervention study assessing the quality of discharge planning before and after the introduction of a discharge coordinator, the coordinator improved the discharge planning process and reduced problems patients experienced after discharge and their perceived need for medical and healthcare services, but there was no evidence of a more timely or effective provision of community services after discharge, or of improved appropriateness or efficiency of bed use.

The intervention evaluated was a discharge coordinator whose sole responsibility was to plan and coordinate the discharge of patients from medical wards, and the study was conducted in the three medical wards at the Homerton Hospital in Hackney, East London.

The study comprised 600 randomly sampled adult patients admitted to the medical wards of the study hospital who were resident in the district (but not in institutions), were under the care of physicians (excluding psychiatry), and were discharged home from one of the medical wards; sampling was conducted in three study phases over 18 months.

Phase I comprised base line data collection; in phase II data were collected after the introduction of the district discharge planning policy and a discharge form (checklist) for all patients; in phase III data were collected after the introduction of the discharge coordinator.

Outcomes assessed were readmission rates, duration of stay, appropriateness of days of care, patients' health and satisfaction, problems after discharge, and receipt of services; patients were interviewed on the ward before discharge and seven to 10 days after being discharged home.

The discharge coordinator resulted in an improved discharge planning process, a reduction in problems experienced by patients after discharge, and a reduction in perceived need for medical and healthcare services; however, there was no evidence that the coordinator resulted in a more timely or effective provision of community services after discharge, or that the appropriateness or efficiency of bed use was improved.

Perforation of the appendix is reported as a risk factor for subsequent tubal infertility, with a risk estimate of 4.8 (95% CI 1.5 to 14.9) in a systematic review of epidemiologic studies on appendectomy and infertility or ectopic pregnancy.

The review's validity assessment concluded that recall bias and poor adjustment for confounding variables in some of the reports weakened the validity of the studies on which this tubal infertility estimate rests.
For ectopic pregnancy, the review yielded a risk estimate of 1.6 (95% CI 1.1 to 2.5) after an appendectomy, which addresses appendectomy in general rather than perforated appendicitis specifically.

The review also noted that recall bias and poor adjustment for confounding variables in some reports weakened the validity of the studies of appendectomy and adverse fertility outcomes, so the ectopic pregnancy estimate is limited by these methodological weaknesses.

In that observational study of patients with ischaemic heart disease attending an urban tertiary referral cardiology centre, 25 suitable patients were enrolled and 107 hypotensive events were documented; 40 ST events occurred in 14 patients, of which a quarter were symptomatic.

Hypotension induced ischaemic (HII) events were defined as episodes of ST segment ischaemia occurring at least one minute after an ambulatory blood pressure measurement (systolic/diastolic) below 100/65 mm Hg during the day, or 90/50 mm Hg at night.

Fourteen HII events occurred in eight patients; 13 of the 14 were preceded by a fall in diastolic pressure (median diastolic pressure 57.5 mm Hg, interquartile range 11, maximum 72 mm Hg, minimum 45 mm Hg) and six were preceded by a fall in systolic pressure (chi(2) = 11.9, p<0.001).

Because the data come from an observational study design, the reported temporal association between ST events and preceding hypotensive events cannot by itself establish that profound hypotension causes myocardial ischaemic events.

Yes — the manic/mixed episode distinction appears to run true over time: over an 11-year period, episodes were consistent (all manic or all mixed) in significantly more patients with bipolar disorder than would be expected by chance.

That comparison used the observed distribution of manic and mixed episodes (N=1,224) among patients with three or more entries in the management information system of a community mental health center (N=241), set against an expected distribution determined by averaging 1,000 randomly generated simulations.

Yes — the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) can favor left hemisphere strokes, because it can award more points for tests of presumed left-hemisphere function, such as language, than for tests of right-hemisphere function, such as neglect.

In a retrospective study of 153 patients with acute stroke seen at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center between January 1995 and March 2000 who underwent MRI and NIHSS within 24 hours of stroke onset, the relationship between acute NIHSS score and stroke volume differed by side.
For patients with NIHSS scores of 0 to 5, the DWI volume of right cerebral lesions was greater than that of left-sided lesions (mean volume 8.8 versus 3.2 cm3; P=0.04).
Among patients with DWI lesions larger than the median volume (9 cm3), 8 of 37 with right-sided stroke had an NIHSS score of 0 to 5 compared with 1 of 39 patients with left-sided stroke (P=0.01).
Multiple linear regression analysis revealed a significantly lower acute NIHSS on the right compared with the left side when adjusted for stroke volume on chronic T2 imaging (P=0.03).

In the placebo arm of the NINDS t-PA stroke trial, the volume for right hemisphere stroke was statistically greater than the volume for left hemisphere stroke when adjusting for the baseline NIHSS (P<0.001).
For each 5-point category of the NIHSS score below 20, the median volume of right hemisphere strokes was approximately double the median volume of left hemisphere strokes.

For patients with a left hemisphere stroke and a 24-hour NIHSS score of 16 to 20, the median volume of cerebral infarction was 48 mL (interquartile range 14 to 111 mL), compared with 133 mL (interquartile range 81 to 208 mL) for patients with a right hemisphere stroke (P<0.001).
The median volume of a right hemisphere stroke was roughly equal to the median volume of a left hemisphere stroke in the next highest 5-point category of the NIHSS.

Yes — outcome could be predicted in children with malignancy and ARDS in a retrospective chart review of 17 children with ARDS and malignancy (mean age 10.5 +/- 5.1 years) who required mechanical ventilation in a pediatric intensive care unit between January 1987 and January 1997: peak inspiratory pressure, positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), and ventilation index values could distinguish outcome by day 3.

In the same cohort, a significant relationship between respiratory data and outcome related to efficiency of oxygenation, as determined by PaO(2)/FIO(2) and P(A-a)O(2), was present from day 8 after onset of mechanical ventilation.

An observational study in a district general hospital of all patients admitted to hospital aged over 75 years with fracture of the proximal femur over 3 1/2 years found that delay in transfer to a rehabilitation ward was associated with a longer total hospital length of stay of 0.64 (95% CI 0.23-1.05) days per day of delay in transfer.

Outcome data collected included the number of patients discharged back to their usual residence and total hospital length of stay, related to age, gender, usual residence and delay in transfer to a rehabilitation ward.
58% of 455 patients were transferred to a rehabilitation ward.

For those patients who were transferred to a rehabilitation ward, only age predicted discharge to a more dependent residence; the relative risk for discharge to a more dependent residence for people aged over 85 years compared to younger people was 1.47 (95% CI 1.15-1.88).

Because the evidence comes from an observational study design, it can demonstrate an association between delay in transfer and longer hospital stay but cannot establish that reducing the delay would itself improve outcomes.

Yes — among dying nursing home residents with documented daily pain, Medicare hospice enrollment was associated with more frequent regular analgesic treatment than nonhospice enrollment: 51% of hospice versus 33% of nonhospice residents received regular treatment for daily pain, and after controlling for clinical confounders hospice residents were about twice as likely to receive it (adjusted odds ratio = 2.08, 95% CI = 1.68–2.56).

This finding comes from a retrospective, comparative cohort study of a daily-pain subset of 709 hospice and 1,326 nonhospice residents drawn from a matched cohort of 2,644 hospice and 7,929 nonhospice nursing home residents in over 800 nursing homes in Kansas, Maine, Mississippi, New York, and South Dakota, whose last Minimum Data Set assessment was completed between 1992 and 1996 and who died before April 1997; analgesic use was taken from detailed drug data on the last MDS before death.

Untreated and potentially inappropriate analgesic use was less common in the hospice group: 15% of hospice residents versus 23% of nonhospice residents in daily pain received no analgesics (OR = 0.57, 95% CI = 0.45–0.74), and a lower proportion of hospice residents (21%) than nonhospice residents (29%) received analgesics not recommended by the American Medical Directors Association (OR = 0.65, 95% CI = 0.52–0.80).

The pattern of drugs differed by group: acetaminophen (not in combination with other drugs) was used most frequently for nonhospice residents (25% of 1,673 prescriptions), whereas morphine derivatives were used most frequently for hospice residents (30% of 1,058 prescriptions).

Because this was a retrospective, comparative cohort design using MDS drug data, it can show an association between hospice enrollment and guideline-concordant analgesic prescribing but cannot establish that hospice enrollment itself causes better pain management; moreover, the reported outcome is a process measure — any recommended analgesic given at least twice a day for each of the 7 days before the last MDS — rather than a measure of pain intensity or relief.
Hepatitis G virus-RNA was detected in 4 out of 23 patients with cryptogenic chronic hepatitis and in 6 out of 40 with hepatitis C virus chronic hepatitis (17.4% vs 15% p=ns).
Demographic and clinical features, including stage and grade of liver histology, were comparable between hepatitis G virus-infected and uninfected subjects.
T virus-DNA was present in serum in 3 subjects, 1 with cryptogenic and 2 with hepatitis C virus-related chronic liver disease.
The study included a total of 23 subjects with chronically raised alanine transaminase and a liver biopsy in whom all known causes of liver disease had been excluded.
The study also included 40 subjects with hepatitis C virus-related chronic liver disease.
TT virus-DNA was present in serum in only 3 subjects, 1 with cryptogenic and 2 with hepatitis C virus-related chronic liver disease.

Yes — the cited physiologic evidence supports that mossy fibers release GABA: mossy fiber terminals show intense immunoreactivity for the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA and for GAD67, and electrical stimuli that recruit dentate granule cells elicit monosynaptic GABAA receptor-mediated synaptic signals in CA3 pyramidal neurons.

The evidence for GABA release by mossy fibers comes from guinea pig hippocampal slices (3- to 5-week-old animals) with whole-cell voltage clamp recordings from CA3 pyramidal cells and stimulating electrodes placed in stratum granulosum and adjusted to recruit mossy fiber-to-CA3 projections, i.e., an ex vivo animal preparation rather than human tissue.

These inhibitory signals satisfy the criteria that distinguish mossy fiber-CA3 synapses: high sensitivity to metabotropic glutamate-receptor agonists, facilitation during repetitive stimulation, and N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor-independent long-term potentiation.
The review's stated purpose is to present physiologic evidence of GABA release by mossy fibers and its modulation by epileptic activity.

Neutrophils isolated from 17 adult blunt major trauma patients (Injury Severity Score > or = 18) at admission (0 hrs) and 8 and 24 hrs later exhibited an enhanced migratory response to high concentrations of interleukin-8 throughout the first 24 hrs of admission, in contrast to the normal physiologic attenuation of migration seen in neutrophils isolated from normal laboratory volunteers (n = 9).

Significantly greater numbers of trauma patients' neutrophils migrated to interleukin-8 concentrations of 30 and 100 ng/mL at each time point when compared with normal volunteers (Mann-Whitney U test, p <.05).

Neutrophil infiltration of the lung is characteristic of early posttraumatic acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and interleukin-8 is elevated in the lung within 2 hrs of major trauma in patients who later develop ARDS, which the source describes as a central role in the recruitment of neutrophils to the lung and their subsequent activation.
Neutrophil counts in the whole blood specimens obtained from trauma patients who later developed ARDS were elevated significantly at admission and declined rapidly throughout the next 24 hrs.

The hypothesis that enhanced interleukin-8-mediated neutrophil migratory activity in the early postinjury phase, before the development of ARDS, may be a crucial factor in the etiology of ARDS was examined in a prospective observational study, a design that can describe the association between posttrauma neutrophil migration and later ARDS but cannot establish that increased neutrophil migratory activity causes ARDS.

Yes — pain appears to be a clinically relevant problem in general adult psychiatry: in a cross-sectional questionnaire study of 106 patients primarily diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder in the field of general adult psychiatry, the point prevalence of pain was about 50%, the 6-month prevalence was 75.5% and the 12-month prevalence was 76.5%.
The most frequent pain complaints among these patients were low back pain, headache, and shoulder and neck pain.

Patients with affective disorders most frequently had pain complaints, followed by those with neurotic, stress-related and somatoform disorders, and then those with psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia, schizotypic and delusional disorders.
Almost 10% of all patients reported pain that continued at least 3 months in the past year, and impairment and unfitness for work were related to the specific psychiatric diagnosis.
Statistically significant risk factors for pain were depression (OR=6.05) and the number of past admissions to psychiatric hospitals (OR=3.609).

Because the study used a cross-sectional questionnaire design, it can establish the prevalence of pain, its duration, associated impairment and unfitness for work, and statistical associations with potential risk factors, but it cannot establish that pain causes, or is caused by, psychiatric disorders.

Patients were divided into 4 groups, on the basis of their pattern of outpatient care over a 12-month period after discharge: 1) general medicine clinic visits only (GM-only); 2) cardiology clinic visits only (CARD-only); 3) general medicine and cardiology (MIXED) clinic visits; and 4) neither general medicine nor cardiology clinic visits (no-GM/CARD).

In a retrospective cohort study conducted with national Veterans Health Administration (VHA) databases, 11,661 patients discharged from VA hospitals between October 1, 1991, and September 30, 1992, with the primary diagnosis of CHF (cohort 1) were examined for the association between the pattern of outpatient care and survival; 1-year survival was evaluated with the Cox proportional hazards model, controlling for clinical and demographic factors.

The overall 1-year mortality rate was 23% in the primary cohort; the unadjusted mortality rate was highest for patients in the no-GM/CARD follow up (29%) and lowest for patients in the MIXED group (19%).

By use of the MIXED group as reference and adjusting for important clinical and demographic factors, the risk of death (risk ratio [95% CI]) was 1.12 (0.94-1.34) in the CARD-only group, 1.26 (1.15-1.38) in the GM-only group, and 1.48 (1.28-1.72) in the no-GM/CARD group.

Consistency of the results was examined by performing identical analysis on a cohort of patients discharged from VHA hospitals between October 1, 1994, and September 30, 1995 (cohort 2, n = 10,141); cohort-2 results were consistent with cohort 1 for most covariates, and significant survival differences were again found between the GM-only and the MIXED group (1.25 [1.14-1.37]).

Because the cited study is an observational retrospective cohort analysis of care patterns rather than a randomized comparison of care settings, its results establish an association between outpatient care pattern and 1-year survival and cannot establish that receiving specialty care itself causes improved survival.
The women were divided into those who received RT around the time of pregnancy and those who were not pregnant.
Comparisons of the overall incidence, actuarial rates, and latency to breast cancer between the two groups were made.
Of the 382 women, 14 developed breast cancer (3.7%).
2.3%, p = 0.0001) and the actuarial rate of breast cancer among the women in the pregnant group (p = 0.011) was statistically significant.
The women treated around the time of pregnancy had a 10- and 15-year actuarial rate of breast cancer of 6.7% and 32.6%, respectively.
The 10-year and 15-year actuarial rate for the nonpregnant women was 0.4% and 1.7%, respectively.
The median latency from RT to the diagnosis of breast cancer was 13.1 and 18.9 years for women in the pregnant and nonpregnant groups, respectively.
In the multivariate analysis, pregnancy around the time of RT was the only variable associated with an increased risk of breast cancer.

The risk was dependent on the length of time from pregnancy to RT, with women receiving RT during pregnancy and within 1 month of pregnancy having an increased risk of breast cancer compared with nonpregnant women and women irradiated later than 1 month after pregnancy (hazard ratio, 22.49; 95% confidence interval, 5.56-90.88; p<0.001).

Cranial CT can distinguish communicating from non-communicating hydrocephalus in tuberculous meningitis only to a limited degree: the sole CT finding that correlated with the type of hydrocephalus was the shape of the third ventricle, so CT does not predict the CSF block level through multiple independent indices.

In that study, a number of CT indices were measured in 50 children with communicating and 34 children with non-communicating hydrocephalus, with the type of hydrocephalus defined according to air-encephalographic findings.
Significantly more children with non-communicating hydrocephalus had a rounded third ventricle than children with communicating hydrocephalus.

Yes — the cited evidence indicates that communication with terminally ill patients can be taught: models of courses that resulted in improvements in participants' communicative skills have been published mainly in the Anglo-American literature, and a 2-day course model based on the first three courses of this kind in Rhineland-Palatinate, attended by 31 participants, was described and analyzed for changes in participants' communication behavior.

In that German course evaluation, participants gave high satisfaction scores for the methods and for the clarity and relevance of the contents; participants' self-assessment on a visual analog scale across seven communication settings showed a growing sense of security, with important increases for communicating a cancer diagnosis with good or less good prognosis, recurrence of cancer, or far advanced cancer without a curative approach, and 3 months after the course participants described multiple changes indicating increased sensibility and professionalism in their communication behavior.
This study was a population-based 13-year follow-up survey of community-dwelling adults living in East Baltimore in 1981.
Subjects were the continuing participants of the Baltimore Epidemiologic Catchment Area Program.
Participants interviewed between 1993 and 1996 with complete data on depressive symptoms and covariates were included (n = 1727).

Using structural equations with a measurement model for dichotomous data (the MIMIC—multiple indicators, multiple causes—model) to compare symptoms between women and men in relation to the nine symptom groups comprising the diagnostic criteria for major depression, adjusting for age, self-reported ethnicity, educational attainment, marital status, and employment, there were no significant gender differences in the self-report of depression symptoms even taking into account the higher level of depressive symptoms of women and the influence of other covariates.

Women were no more likely to endorse sadness than were men, as evidenced by a direct effect coefficient that was not significantly different from the null [adjusted estimated direct effect of gender on report of sadness = 0.105, 95% confidence interval (-0.113, 0.323)].

In two different human ovary cancer cell lines, a significant additive effect of 2-methoxyestradiol with epirubicine and with carboplatin was observed at the lower concentration range of these chemotherapeutic substances.

In that in vitro model, all cell lines were incubated with equimolar concentrations of 2-methoxyestradiol (0.8-25 microM) and the chemotherapeutics epirubicine, doxorubicine, paclitaxel, docetaxel, carboplatin, vinorelbine, 5-fluorouracil and mafosfamide, with proliferation measured after four days using the ATP-chemosensitivity test.
Because the reported combination testing was performed in human ovary cancer cell lines in vitro, the design cannot demonstrate that chemotherapeutic dosages given to patients can be reduced.

In uveal melanoma, c-kit expression was found in 84 of 134 paraffin-embedded tumour samples by immunohistochemistry and in six of eight fresh-frozen samples by Western blot analysis. c-Kit was strongly expressed and tyrosine phosphorylated in cultured uveal melanoma cells (OCM-1, OCM-3 and 92-1) compared with cutaneous melanoma cells, and in contrast to cutaneous melanoma cell lines it maintained a high phosphorylation level in serum-depleted uveal melanoma cells.

Expression of the stem cell growth factor (c-kit ligand) was detected in all three uveal melanoma cell lines, suggesting autocrine (paracrine) stimulation pathways, while no activation-related mutations were found in exon 11 of the KIT gene.

Treatment of uveal melanoma cell lines with STI571, which blocks c-kit autophosphorylation, resulted in cell death, and the IC(50) of the inhibitory effects on c-kit phosphorylation and on cell proliferation was of equal size and less than 2.5 microM, indicating that c-kit is a potential therapeutic target in uveal melanoma.

The evidence that reducing spasticity translates into functional benefit is mixed: an exploratory meta-analysis pooling individual stroke-patient data from two randomised controlled trials of intramuscular botulinum toxin reported a definite relationship between the maximum change in spasticity and the maximum change in arm function independent of treatment (rho = -0.2822, p = 0.0008, n = 137), yet noted that although botulinum toxin is used to reduce spasticity, its functional benefits are less easily demonstrated.

In that pooled analysis, maximum changes in both the composite spasticity and composite functional measures occurred concurrently in 47 patients, whereas in 26 patients the improvement in spasticity preceded the improvement in function and 18 showed the reverse.

The relationship between change in spasticity and change in arm function was clear in patients treated with botulinum toxin (Dysport) at 500 or 1000 units (rho = -0.5679, p = 0.0090, n = 22; rho = -0.4430, p = 0.0018, n = 47), but was not present in those treated with placebo or 1500 units.

In a separate trial, both groups showed significant improvement of spasticity with a median Modified Ashworth Scale of 1+ (range, 0.0-2.0) at eight weeks, yet compared with baseline no significant differences between the two groups were detected in any of the surface electromyography and clinical parameters at week 8 (P>0.05).

As an exploratory meta-analysis of change scores and their timing from pooled trial data, this design can describe an association between reductions in spasticity and changes in arm function but cannot establish that reducing spasticity causes functional benefit.

In a prospective survey of general practitioner referrals to private and NHS consultant-led services between 1 January and 31 December 2001 from 10 general practices in the Trent Focus Collaborative Research Network, United Kingdom, 90.4% (15,495) of 17,137 referrals were to the NHS and 9.6% (1,642) were to the private sector, with referrals aggregated to private and NHS referral rates for each electoral ward in each practice.

The NHS referral rate was significantly higher in wards whose private referral rates were in the top fifth compared with wards in the bottom fifth (rate ratio 1.40, 95% CI 1.15 to 1.71, p = 0.001) after adjustment for deprivation and practice; private referral rates were lower in the most deprived fifth of wards than in the least deprived fifth (rate ratio 0.25, 95% CI 0.15 to 0.41, p<0.001), while NHS referral rates were slightly higher in the most deprived fifth (rate ratio 1.18, 95% CI 0.98 to 1.42, p = 0.08), both after age standardisation and adjustment for practice.

Because this evidence comes from ward-level referral rates measured within a single year rather than from repeated measures over time, it cannot show whether an increase in private health care use over time reduces NHS demand.

On the reported comparison, decisional algorithms cannot replace WHO global introspection (GI) for individual causality assessment of spontaneously reported ADRs, because the algorithms tested showed a high average sensitivity of 93% and positive predictive value of 89% but a low average specificity of 7% with a negative predictive value of 31%.
In that study, an expert panel assessed the causality of 500 adverse reports using the WHO global introspection method, and the same reports were independently assessed using 15 published algorithms.

For the comparison, the causality assessment level 'possible' was considered the lower limit for a report to be considered drug related, with sensitivity defined as the proportion of reports classified as drug related by both the algorithm and the GI method and specificity as the proportion simultaneously considered non-drug related; the analysis was performed for the total sample and within serious or unexpected events.

Yes — in a French study of 48 scenarios, lay people and psychologists found it much more acceptable than physicians to breach confidentiality to protect the wife of a patient with a sexually transmitted disease: breaching confidentiality was accepted by 144 lay people, 10 psychologists and 7 physicians, with mean ratings of 11.76 for lay people, 9.28 for psychologists and 2.90 for physicians on a 0-22 scale.

In the same French study the scenarios were all combinations of five factors (severity of disease, time taken to discuss it, the patient's intent to inform the spouse, intent to adopt protective behaviours, and decision to consult an STD expert; 2 x 2 x 3 x 2 x 2), and the patient's stated intentions to protect his wife and to inform her of the disease had the greatest impact on acceptability.

A cluster analysis of the 144 lay participants identified subgroups finding breaching confidentiality 'always acceptable' (n = 14), 'depending on the many circumstances' (n = 87), requiring 'consultation with an expert' (n = 30), and 'never acceptable' (n = 13).

Because the reported figures are acceptability ratings for hypothetical scenarios rather than observations of actual practice, the study design cannot establish whether physicians would in fact breach confidentiality in such situations.

Preoperative TBS changed the diagnosis in a subset of newborns with esophageal atresia: among 62 patients who underwent preoperative TBS between 1997 and 2003, the pre-TBS Gross classification was type A in 9, type B in none and type C in 51, yet at TBS 3 of the 9 type A patients were found to have an unsuspected proximal fistula (type B).
TBS also detected respiratory tree malformations that had not been identified previously in 4 patients (2 aberrant right upper bronchus and 2 hypoplastic bronchi).

TBS findings directly altered the surgical approach: when a wide carinal fistula was found it was mechanically occluded with a Fogarty catheter and cannulated with rigid bronchoscopy, and the 3 patients with an unsuspected proximal fistula plus the 2 with an H-type fistula were repaired through a cervical approach.

Carinal fistulas in 14 type C patients were occluded by Fogarty catheter to improve ventilation during repair, and overall TBS was judged clinically useful in 28 of 62 patients (45.2%), including 15 of 62 (24.2%) in whom it was crucial in modifying the surgical approach.
No complications of preoperative TBS were observed in this series of 62 newborns with esophageal atresia.

Occlusion of the atherosclerotic ascending aorta with an endoaortic inflatable balloon has been proposed as an alternative to conventional cross-clamping to prevent injury to the vessel and distal embolization of debris; in the reported series the surgeon's choice was based on preoperative identification of aortic calcifications or intraoperative epiaortic ultrasonographic scanning, and endoaortic occlusion was employed in 52 of 2,172 consecutive patients.

In the single cited series of endoaortic balloon occlusion used for the atherosclerotic ascending aorta, the evidence indicates the technique was not safe: in-hospital death occurred in 13 of the 52 treated patients (25%), a rate significantly higher than among all other patients (4.2%, p<0.0001) and higher than the expected European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation estimate (10.5%, p=0.05).
Use of endoaortic occlusion was independently associated with in-hospital death on multivariable analysis (odds ratio 5.609, 95% confidence interval 2.684 to 11.719).
In 10 patients (19.2%) the endoaortic balloon had to be replaced by the ordinary cross-clamp because of incomplete occlusion (n = 5), hindered exposure (n = 2), or balloon rupture (n = 3).

Stroke on awakening from anesthesia occurred in 2 patients (3.8%); the stroke rate was higher in the endoaortic occlusion group than among all other patients, but the difference was only possibly significant (3.8% versus 0.8%, p = 0.067).

The clinical significance of bile duct sludge does not clearly differ from that of common bile duct stones with respect to recurrence after endoscopic therapy: among 228 patients who underwent therapeutic ERCP for suspected choledocholithiasis, CBD stones recurred in 17% (33/197) of patients with CBD stones versus 16% (5/31) of patients with bile duct sludge (p = 0.99).

Bile duct sludge occurred in 14% (31/228) of these patients and was more common in females; common bile duct dilation was less common in the sludge group, and the other known risk factors for recurrent CBD stones (age, previous open cholecystectomy, bile duct angulation, and the presence of a peripampullary diverticulum) were not statistically different between the sludge and stone groups.

The significance of bile duct sludge is poorly defined, and this study was designed to compare bile duct sludge with bile duct stones in terms of frequency, associated risk factors, and clinical outcome after endoscopic therapy.

Yes — in 300 patients with Type 1 diabetes (158 male; HbA(1c) median 8.2%, range 5.2-12.8%; median age 36 years, range 16-88; diabetes duration 14.5 years, range 2-49), none taking renin-angiotensin system blocking drugs, serum ACE showed a statistically significant but clinically weak relationship with severe hypoglycaemia (SH) incidence.

Participants recorded how often they had experienced SH, and glycated haemoglobin (HbA(1c)) and serum ACE were measured; the difference in SH incidence between ACE activity quartiles and the serum ACE-SH relationship were examined with non-parametric statistical tests and a negative binomial model.

The overall incidence of SH was 0.93 episodes per patient year, and the mean incidence in the top versus bottom quartiles of ACE activity was 0.5 versus 1.7 episodes per patient year, a difference that was not statistically significant (P = 0.075).

Spearman's test showed a very weak but statistically significant association between serum ACE level and SH incidence (r = 0.115, P = 0.047), and the binomial model likewise showed a statistically significant (P = 0.002) though clinically weak relationship between serum ACE and SH.
In total, 38 adults (age range 20-72 years; mean age of 36 years) with ID participated in the study; IQs ranged from 45 to 69 with a mean IQ of 58.
The intervention programme involved 15 weekly lessons of 1 h each, taught during 3 months.

In this study, teaching text comprehension strategies improved reading comprehension: direct programme effects - as determined by posttest-pretest contrasts for strategy tests - were substantial, except for the questioning strategy.
The transfer effect to general text comprehension was even more substantial than the direct effects, and the results on this test were well maintained at a follow-up test.
Results indicated no significant difference between group and individual instruction conditions.

Compared with tamoxifen for early breast cancer, aromatase inhibitors were associated with an unexpectedly greater number of grade 3 and 4 cardiovascular events (CVAEs), as defined by National Cancer Institute of Canada-Common Toxicity Criteria version 2.0.

Yes—breast cancer prognosis appears to be inherited: in a population-based Swedish cohort, daughters and sisters of a proband with poor 5-year prognosis had a 60% higher 5-year breast cancer mortality than relatives of a proband with good prognosis (hazard ratio 1.6; 95% CI 1.2 to 2.2; p for trend 0.002), after adjustment for potential confounders.

The same cohort, drawn from the nationwide Swedish Multi-Generation Register, comprised 2,787 mother-daughter pairs and 831 sister pairs with breast cancer diagnosed from 1961 to 2001, with complete follow-up and proband 5-year prognosis classified into poor, intermediary, or good tertiles.

The 5-year survival proportion was 87% among daughters whose mothers died within 5 years versus 91% if the mother was alive (p = 0.03), and among sisters the corresponding proportions were 70% versus 88% (p = 0.001).

The association between a proband's poor prognosis and a relative's 5-year breast cancer mortality was slightly stronger among sisters (HR 1.8; 95% CI 1.0 to 3.4) than among daughters (HR 1.6; 95% CI 1.1 to 2.3).

Because this is an observational population-based cohort study of familial aggregation, it documents that a proband's prognosis predicts breast cancer mortality in daughters and sisters, but the design alone cannot separate inherited traits from shared non-genetic factors as the explanation for the familial clustering.

In a retrospective review of 56 patients aged 11 to 216 months who underwent exploration for a nonpalpable testis at two institutions between 1994 and 2006 and had removal of the testicular remnant, viable germ cell elements were identified in 8 of the specimens (14%), and an additional 4 patients (7%) had seminiferous tubules without germ cell elements.

The optimal management of the testicular remnant associated with the vanishing testes syndrome is controversial, with some urologists advocating surgical exploration and others considering it unnecessary, the differing opinions being based on variable reports of viable germ cell elements found within the testicular remnants; the authors reviewed their experience to better understand the pathology of the syndrome and the need for surgical management.

Yes — in winter oil-seed rape (Brassica napus subsp. oleifera), pectins are implicated in cold acclimation: in leaves of two double-haploid lines differing in winter survival and blackleg (Leptosphaeria maculans) resistance, acclimation at 2 degrees C retarded leaf expansion while freezing resistance developed, and these effects were associated with increases in leaf tensile stiffness, cell wall and pectin contents, pectin methylesterase (EC 3.1.1.11) activity and low-methylated pectin content, independently of genotype.
The cold-induced modifications in cell wall properties were more pronounced in the leaves of the more pathogen-resistant genotype.

Pectins are also implicated in de-acclimation of winter oil-seed rape: de-acclimation promoted leaf expansion and reversed most of the cold-induced effects, with the exception of pectin methylesterase activity, which remained altered.

In a retrospective immunohistochemical study of paraffin-embedded biopsies from 125 patients with HBV infection (25 patients each with mild, moderate or severe hepatitis, cirrhosis or HCC) using an anti c-kit monoclonal antibody, the greatest number of c-kit-positive cases and the higher intensity of staining were found in the livers of patients with severe hepatitis and HCC, and in chronic hepatitis B infection the staining intensity was parallel with the grade and stage of the disease.
In cirrhotic liver, a lower intensity of staining and rarely c-kit positivity were present, and in the areas where fibrosis was seen c-kit positivity was rare or absent.

In the HCC specimens, c-kit positivity appeared both inside and around the cancerous nodes, and c-kit expression was observed in 62 of 75 HCC tissue specimens (82%) (p<0.001); in addition, 50 further HCC specimens formed on an HBV basis were studied to determine the prevalence of c-kit overexpression.

In the whole group only a slight difference was found between both training modalities concerning their writing abilities, so the whole-group comparison does not indicate that specialized phonological awareness training is warranted for every preschool child.

The indication appears to differ across children: those with a history of hearing loss, actual hearing loss or pathologic middle ear findings profited most from the specialized training program compared with the control group in their reading abilities.

In a retrospective review of liver biopsies from a 10-year period at one hospital, routine laboratory markers were useful for distinguishing nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) from alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH): a multivariate model combining MCV, the AST/ALT ratio and sex achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.92.

Of the 95 patients with steatohepatitis identified, NASH was diagnosed in 58 (61%; 30 female) and ASH in 37 (39%; 9 female), with the diagnosis assigned on the basis of biopsy and history of alcohol consumption (<140 g/week) after other liver diseases were excluded.

An AST/ALT ratio >1 was more common in ASH than in NASH (54.1% vs 20.7%, P = 0.0008), as was high-grade fibrosis (59% vs 19%, P < 0.0001); the AST/ALT ratio (P < 0.0001) and age (P = 0.00049) were independent predictors of high-grade fibrosis.
MCV was elevated in 53% of ASH patients and was normal in all NASH patients (P < 0.0001), and differences in MCV were more marked in high-grade fibrosis.
On multivariate analysis, MCV (P = 0.0013), the AST/ALT ratio (P = 0.011) and sex (P = 0.0029) were identified as relevant regressors, giving an aROC of 0.92.

Because the study was a retrospective re-evaluation of data collected prior to biopsy, with diagnoses assigned from histology and reported alcohol intake, it supports an association between these routine parameters and the type of steatohepatitis rather than demonstrating that acting on them alters clinical outcomes.

For tissue microarrays, although pathologists frequently feel better if larger core sizes are used, there is no evidence in the literature showing that large cores are better (or worse) than small cores for assessment of TMAs; measurement of a single random 0.6-mm spot was comparable to analysis of the whole 1-mm or 1.5-mm spot, with a Pearson R coefficient varying from 0.87 to 0.98 for all markers tested.
Evidence from surgery shows that high volume is often associated with better outcomes.

In the study of boys and girls, overweight and obese girls selected larger ideal body figures than the others (trend test: P<0.001); compared with those with middle ideal body figures, girls who selected smaller ones were twice as likely to have an unhealthy diet as indicated by less fruit and milk consumption, with odds ratios (95% CIs) of 2.40 (1.15-5.02) for fruit intake less than once per week and 2.13 (1.06-4.29) for milk consumption less than once per day.

Boys with larger IBI were less likely to eat snack often [≥once/day; OR = 0.11 (0.02-0.50)]; girls with larger IBI were less likely to spend more screen time [OR = 0.12 (0.02-0.70)] and reported better food choice intentions (P<0.05); overweight and obese boys and girls appeared to have better food choice intentions and food self-efficacy than their non-overweight peers (trend test: both P<0.01).

In a survey, two hundred and nine (57% female) adults completed the survey; thirty eight percent had a healthy BMI (18.5-24.9), 38% were overweight (BMI 25-29.9) and a further 22% were obese (BMI>30); over 80% thought being overweight was likely or very likely to be a risk factor for cardiovascular disease, hypertension, diabetes and stroke; however, 20% of overweight or obese individuals did not think their health would improve if they lost weight.

Yes — in a retrospective series of 154 adults undergoing major foregut surgery, laparoscopic surgery was associated with a lower risk of new-onset atrial fibrillation (univariate p = 0.004), and the association persisted in multivariate analysis after adjusting for surgery type (OR 0.09, 95% CI 0.01-0.95, p = 0.04).

The cohort comprised 154 adult patients who underwent major foregut surgery including esophagectomy, partial or total gastrectomy, redo Heller myotomy, and redo or transthoracic fundoplications; 14 of the 154 developed new-onset atrial fibrillation, nonthoracic surgery was also associated with lower risk of atrial fibrillation (p = 0.01), atrial fibrillation was associated with age (OR 1.08, 95% CI 1.02-1.14, p = 0.01), and patients with atrial fibrillation were older (67.1 +/- 8.8 years versus 56.4 +/- 14.1 years, p = 0.006).

Because the data came from a retrospective record review rather than a randomized comparison, the reported lower risk of atrial fibrillation with laparoscopic surgery is an association and cannot establish that performing laparoscopic rather than open surgery itself reduces the incidence of this complication.

In a retrospective cohort of 42 pregnancies with severe Kell alloimmunization in which fetal platelet counts were obtained before the first intrauterine transfusion, the cited evidence indicates that Kell alloimmunization was not associated with clinically significant fetal thrombocytopenia, since none of the Kell fetuses, including 15 with severe hydrops, had a platelet count below 50 x 10(9)/l.

Fetal thrombocytopenia defined as a platelet count below 150 x 10(9)/l was found in 4/42 (10%) of the Kell alloimmunized pregnancies versus 84/318 (26%) of the RhD alloimmunized control pregnancies, whose platelet counts came from 318 first intrauterine transfusions.

Among the RhD alloimmunized pregnancies, clinically significant thrombocytopenia (platelet count below 50 x 10(9)/l) occurred in 2/230 (1%) of non-hydropic fetuses and 7/30 (23%) of severely hydropic fetuses, the comparison group against which the Kell findings were assessed.

In a secondary analysis of an ongoing prospective multicenter cohort of 1,036 blunt-injured adults with hemorrhagic shock, separate Cox proportional hazard regression models based on all patients evaluated the effects of gender on mortality, multiple organ failure, and nosocomial infection after controlling for all important confounders.
For the entire cohort of 1,036 patients, overall mortality was 20%, multiple organ failure 40%, and nosocomial infection 45%.

Men (n = 680) and women (n = 356) were clinically similar except that men required higher crystalloid volumes, more often had a history of alcoholism and liver disease, and had greater ventilatory and intensive care unit requirements.
Female gender was independently associated with a 43% lower risk of multiple organ failure and a 23% lower risk of nosocomial infection.

The study was designed to characterize the gender dimorphism after injury with specific reference to the reproductive age of the women (young, <48 years, vs old, >52 years) in a cohort of severely injured trauma patients in which significant variation in postinjury care was minimized.

The regression models were then used to characterize the effect of gender in the young and old age groups, and gender remained an independent risk factor in both subgroup analyses, with the protection afforded by female gender remaining unchanged.

Because the dimorphism was characterized by comparing young (<48 years) with old (>52 years) women rather than by reporting measured hormone levels, the analysis as designed cannot establish that hormonal differences are responsible for the observed protection.

Yes — home sampling kits for bacterial sexually transmitted infections were generally viewed as acceptable, that is, positively, by men who have sex with men in the cited qualitative study, which was conducted as a formative evaluation of HSKs using focus groups (n = 20) and one-to-one semi-structured interviews (n = 24).

The reported benefits of a HSK were increased access to testing, enhanced personal comfort and empowerment, while the concerns raised were the accuracy of the test, delays in receiving results, a possible lack of support and a potential negative impact on 'others'.

Because the evidence comes from focus group discussions of self-sampling materials and interviews with men who had used self-sampling in a pilot clinical study, the findings describe views and potential acceptability rather than measured uptake of home sampling kits; the reported perspectives cannot by themselves establish use or test performance.

Yes, in a swine extremity arterial injury model, direct application of the zeolite mineral QuikClot Advanced Clotting Sponge (QC-ACS) over the lacerated femoral artery decreased total blood loss compared with a control group given a pressure dressing with manual pressure over a gauze sponge.

In the same study of 16 swine (control n=6, QC n=10) with a 5 mm femoral artery incision, QC application led to a slower drop in blood pressure, while the control group had a significantly higher increase in lactate within 60 minutes and a significantly increased mean prothrombin time at 60 minutes; the QC group had significantly higher hematocrit levels.

The cited evidence is mixed: in a retrospective series of 145 patients with gallbladder polyps, neoplastic polyps were more frequently found in patients with a rapid growth rate greater than 0.6 mm/mo, but on multivariate analysis the growth rate was not related to the neoplastic nature of a polyp.

In that study, the growth rate was determined from the change in size per time interval between 2 ultrasonographic examinations (mm/mo), and the 145 patients with gallbladder polyps were retrospectively investigated at Samsung Medical Center, South Korea, from 1994 to 2007, having undergone at least 1 ultrasonographic follow-up examination over an interval greater than 6 months before cholecystectomy.

On multivariate analysis, older age (>60 y) and large polyp size (>10 mm) were significantly associated with neoplastic polyps, whereas the growth rate was not, and neoplastic polyps were also more frequently found in patients with hypertension and in those with a polyp size greater than 10 mm.

A case report describes cerebro-mediastinal tuberculosis in an immuno-competent child, a seven-year-old girl, an occurrence the authors state had not been previously described, and the child described also had a probable Say-Barber-Miller syndrome.

The child presented with infantile encephalopathy since birth characterized by facial dysmorphy evocative of a bird face, microcephaly and mental retardation, together with recurrent infections and several months of back pain with anorexia and weight loss.

Spinal and cerebral MRI showed a mediastinal mass involving the spine and cerebral lesions evocative of tuberculomas, the tuberculin interdermal reaction was positive, and culture of a vertebral biopsy was positive for Koch bacillus.
Anti-tuberculosis treatment improved the child's general and local status.

No established causative link is reported between probable Say-Barber-Miller syndrome and cerebromediastinal tuberculosis; the report only discusses a putative causative link between the syndrome and the occurrence of tuberculosis, and notes that an extensive immunological work-up was normal.

Because the evidence is a single descriptive case report, the proposed association between the probable Say-Barber-Miller syndrome and the occurrence of tuberculosis cannot by itself establish causation.

The cited evidence is mixed rather than a clear yes or no: in a retrospective national sample of veterans with ischemic stroke, overall performance was above 70% for 10 of the 14 inpatient quality indicators examined, yet older patients were less likely than younger patients to receive several specific processes of care.

Inpatient stroke care quality was assessed across 14 processes of care: dysphagia screening, NIHSS score documentation, thrombolysis, deep venous thrombosis prophylaxis, antithrombotic therapy by hospital day 2 and at discharge, early ambulation, fall risk assessment, pressure ulcer risk assessment, rehabilitation needs assessment, atrial fibrillation management, lipid management, smoking cessation counseling, and stroke education.

The study was a retrospective national sample of veterans admitted to 129 Veterans Affairs medical centers for ischemic stroke during fiscal year 2007, comprising 3,939 veterans whose mean age was 67.8 years (standard deviation, 11.5).

In unadjusted analyses, older patients were less likely than younger patients to receive lipid management, smoking cessation, NIHSS documentation, and early ambulation, while older patients were more likely to receive dysphagia screening and stroke education.

After adjustment for demographic, clinical, and hospital-level characteristics, age-related differences in processes of care were less consistent, although the youngest patients were more likely to receive smoking cessation counseling and the oldest patients were less likely to receive lipid management.

Because the evidence comes from a retrospective study of inpatient process measures among veterans with ischemic stroke treated in Veterans Affairs medical centers, it cannot establish whether stroke care is adequate for older patients across all settings, care processes, and clinical outcomes; this is a limitation entailed by the study design, not a reported outcome.

Yes, ESC could change the way people drive: although research indicates ESC reduces collision rates and saves lives, drivers may show behavioral adaptation to or overreliance on ESC that could offset or reduce its overall effectiveness.

In a Canadian telephone survey of 1017 owners/drivers of 2006-2008 ESC-equipped passenger vehicles in Quebec and British Columbia, 23% of ESC owners who knew their vehicle had ESC reported noticing long-lasting changes in their driving behavior since they began driving that vehicle.

Interpretation: these figures come from drivers' self-reported perceptions in telephone surveys, a design that documents reported awareness and perceived behavior change rather than measured driving behavior, so it cannot establish that ESC actually alters how people drive.

The trial of fenofibrate in sleep apnoea was a proof-of-concept study consisting of a placebo run-in period of 1 week (5 weeks if fibrate washout was required) followed by a 4-week randomized, double-blind treatment period, in which 34 subjects with diagnosed sleep apnoea syndrome not treated with continuous positive airways pressure (mean age 55 years, BMI 34 kg/m2, fasting triglycerides 3.5 mmol/L) were randomized to once-daily fenofibrate 145 mg NanoCrystal tablet or placebo; overnight polysomnography, computerized attention/vigilance tests and blood sampling for lipids, insulin, fasting plasma glucose and fibrinogen were performed at the end of each study period, and because the study was exploratory a range of sleep variables was evaluated.

The investigators characterized the design as an exploratory study in patients with mild to moderate sleep apnoea with limited treatment duration, concomitant hypnotic treatment in 35% of patients and no correction for multiplicity of testing.
Fenofibrate produced no significant change in the apnoea/hypopnoea index, with a reduction versus control of 14% (95% CI -47 to 40%, p = 0.533).

Fenofibrate significantly reduced the percentage of time with SpO(2)<90%, from 9.0% to 3.5% compared with 10.0% to 11.5% on placebo (p = 0.007), and reduced obstructive apnoeas by 44%, from 18.5 at baseline to 15.0 at end of treatment versus 29.0 to 30.5 on placebo (p = 0.048), as well as non-cortical micro-awakenings per hour, from 23.5 to 18.0 versus 24.0 to 25.0 with placebo (p = 0.004).
Other sleep variables evaluated in the trial were not significantly influenced by fenofibrate.

In that study, 30 guinea pigs were divided into a control group, a halofantrine therapeutic dose group and a halofantrine double therapeutic dose group, with one cochlea per animal stained with haematoxylin and eosin and the other with toluidine blue.
No changes were detected in the control group.
The halofantrine therapeutic dose group showed loss and distortion of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells, and loss of spiral ganglia cells.
In the halofantrine double therapeutic dose group, the inner and outer hair cells were distorted and there was loss of spiral ganglia cells.

The authors state that there have been no studies investigating halofantrine's effect on hearing, and the drug's introduction has been delayed because of possible side effects and insufficient studies of adverse reactions in humans.

Because the reported findings are histological changes in guinea pig cochleae rather than audiometric or functional hearing measurements in humans, they cannot by themselves establish that halofantrine causes hearing loss or hearing impairment in patients.

In Texas during 1995-2005, African-American and Hispanic women generally experienced higher breast cancer mortality than White non-Hispanics, with these differences especially significant in the southeast metropolitan areas and the southwest border of Texas.

Geographic scale mattered for detecting racial disparities in breast cancer mortality: the proportion and location of significant disparities changed depending on the type of statistic used (relative risk versus risk difference) and the geographic level examined (census tract, zip code, or county).
The largest proportion of significant results was observed for the risk difference statistic combined with census tract data.

Racial disparities were quantified using both relative (RR) and absolute (RD) statistics that account for population size and correct for the unreliable rates typically observed for minority groups and smaller geographic units.

The cited evidence indicates that prostate specific antigen does not need to be adjusted for body mass index: in 994 men (4,937 observations) without prostate cancer in the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging, body mass index was not significantly associated with prostate specific antigen after adjusting for age (p = 0.06), and a 10-point body mass index increase corresponded to a prostate specific antigen difference of only -0.03 ng/ml (95% CI -0.40-0.49).

In the same longitudinal aging study, results were similar when men with prostate cancer were included, when percent body fat was substituted for body mass index, and after adjusting for prostate volume, and longitudinal weight changes also had no significant association with prostate specific antigen; separate models explored men with prostate cancer censored at diagnosis, percent body fat measurements, weight changes with time, and adjustment for initial prostate size in 483 men (2,523 observations) with pelvic magnetic resonance imaging measurements.

In a separate cohort of 6,103 men who had a 2-year biopsy, of whom 1,646 (27%) were normal weight, 3,209 (53%) overweight and 1,248 (20%) obese, mean adjusted prostate specific antigen for normal weight, overweight and obese subjects was 7.73, 7.17 and 6.79 ng/ml on placebo (p-trend = 0.192) and 3.16, 2.93 and 2.62 ng/ml on dutasteride (p = 0.008).

In that study, AUC analysis using raw prostate specific antigen data for predicting prostate cancer ranged from 0.60 to 0.64 in the placebo arm and 0.58 to 0.66 in the dutasteride arm with no difference across body mass index categories (p-interactions ≥ 0.212), and similar results were found for high grade prostate cancer with AUC ranging from 0.69 to 0.70 in the placebo arm and 0.65 to 0.75 in the dutasteride arm but no differences across body mass index categories (p-interactions ≥ 0.157).

In a retrospective single-institution analysis of 692 women at 24-32 weeks' gestation who received antenatal corticosteroids (AC), continuation of pregnancy was short in most cases: 321 (46.4%) delivered within 1 week of AC, 92 of those women (13.3%) within 24 hours, and only 124 (17.9%) remained pregnant 1 week after AC and delivered before 34 weeks.
Two hundred forty-seven of the 692 women (35.7%) delivered at 34 weeks' gestation or later.

The study was designed to determine the duration of continuing pregnancy after AC administration and to evaluate the potential opportunity for rescue AC; the 124 women who remained pregnant 1 week after AC and delivered before 34 weeks were compared with women who delivered more than 2 weeks after AC but at 34 weeks or later.

Women were more likely to deliver before 34 weeks if they had received AC for premature preterm rupture of membranes (OR 3.83, 95% CI 2.06-7.17), for twins (OR 2.90, 95% CI 1.42-5.95), or before 28 weeks' gestation (OR 2.21, 95% CI 1.38-3.52).

Because this was a retrospective observational analysis, the reported proportions describe the timing of delivery after the initial AC course and identify a potential window for rescue AC; they cannot establish that administering a rescue course improves outcomes.

Yes — endometrial polyp formation is associated with increased expression of both VEGF and TGF-β1: in a prospective study of 70 premenopausal women, VEGF and TGF-β1 scores were significantly higher in endometrial polyps than in adjacent endometrial tissue, with the pattern of significance differing by cell type (glandular vs stromal) and by menstrual phase.

The study compared VEGF and TGF-β1 expression between endometrial polyps and adjacent endometrial tissue in 70 premenopausal women, and the comparison was made separately for endometrium specimens obtained in the proliferative and secretory phases.

The VEGF score in glandular cells of endometrial polyps was significantly higher than in adjacent endometrium in both the proliferative phase (P<0.001) and the secretory phase (P=0.03), whereas the VEGF score in stromal cells of polyps was significantly higher than in adjacent endometrium only in the proliferative phase (P=0.006).

The TGF-β1 score in glandular cells of endometrial polyps was significantly higher than in adjacent endometrium in the proliferative phase (P=0.02), while the TGF-β1 score in stromal cells of polyps was significantly higher than in adjacent endometrium in both the proliferative phase (P=0.006) and the secretory phase (P=0.008).

Yes, partly: in the Swiss National Cohort, men appeared to benefit more from being married than women with respect to mortality in middle age, but after adjustment for living arrangements the gender difference by marital status disappeared.

The benefit of being married was stronger for men than for women, yet mortality patterns were similar between genders, with higher mortality among divorced and single individuals than among widowed individuals below age 80.

The analysis used longitudinal Swiss National Cohort data linking 1990 census records to mortality data up to 2005 for all residents over age 44 years in Switzerland (n=2,440,242), with all-cause mortality hazard ratios for marital status and living arrangements estimated by Cox regression separately for men and women and different age groups, adjusted for education and socio-professional category.

Stratification by living arrangement showed the highest mortality risks among 45-64-year-old divorced men living alone (HR 1.72, 95% CI 1.67 to 1.76) and single men living alone (HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.63 to 1.71).
Among women of the same 45-64 age group, the highest mortality risk was observed for those who were single and living with a partner (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.58 to 1.82).
In older age groups the impact of marital status decreased.

As an observational census-linked cohort analysis, the reported hazard ratios describe associations between marital status, living arrangement and all-cause mortality and do not by themselves establish that changing marital status or living arrangement would alter mortality risk.

The evidence is mixed: elderly and younger cancer patients differ in some care needs and treatment attitudes, but a cross-sectional survey of patients aged 35-82 (subgroups ≤65 vs ≥66 years) found few significant differences between the two age subgroups apart from issues such as the need for intimacy and support.

In that survey, the requests most frequently expressed by the older group were financial-insurance information (73.9%), the need to talk to people with the same illness (71.7%), the need for more comprehensible information from doctors and nurses (71.7%), and the need for better dialogue with clinicians (69.6%).

Because this needs survey was an observational cross-sectional study, its age-related differences in expressed needs describe associations and cannot establish that changing care delivery by age would improve outcomes.
In a comparison of cohorts aged <65 years and 65+ years, disease diagnosis differed between the cohorts (P<0.001) while treatment modalities were similar (P = 0.28).

There was no difference between the <65 and 65+ cohorts in the desire for surgery offering a chance of disease cure (P = 0.75), except that the elderly desired cure more when treatment was associated with disfigurement (P = 0.029).

Issues of sexuality and femininity associated with gynecologic cancer and treatment were more important to younger patients (P<0.001), whereas the elderly supported equality of care with relation to age more strongly than the young and believed more strongly that doctors should make management decisions (P<0.001).

In a cross-sectional household survey of women residing in rural areas and in their 0-12 months after childbirth from 30 rural townships, none of six dimensions and total score of quality of life displayed significant difference between women with normal delivery and caeserean section.
The overall caeserean section rate was 70·0% (962/1375), and most of them (59·7%) were selected by maternal request.

Postpartum quality of life was assessed with the scale for rural postnatal quality of life across six dimensions: physical complaints and pain, sleep and energy, sex satisfaction, interpersonal communication, self-evaluated living stress and perceived life satisfaction.

Because the study used a cross-sectional design, it can describe the absence of an association between delivery mode and postpartum quality of life but cannot establish that changing delivery mode would cause a change in women's postpartum quality of life.

Yes — the EQ-5D showed construct validity in patients with acute coronary syndrome: in a cross-sectional study conducted at Trakya University Hospital between February and May 2008, 122 patients completed the Turkish version of the EQ-5D and the MacNew heart-related quality of life scale, and construct validity of the EQ-5D was assessed through its relationships with MacNew subscales using Spearman rank correlation and multiple linear regression analyses.

In that acute coronary syndrome sample, the mean EQ-5D index score was 0.79±0.32 and the MacNew global score was 5.01±1.16; EQ-5D index scores correlated with MacNew subscales at 0.557 to 0.721 and EQ-5D VAS scores at 0.297 to 0.484 (p<0.001 for all), and in the stepwise regression model the MacNew global score was a significant factor for the EQ-5D index score (β=0.188; 95% CI 0.152-0.224; p<0.001).

Because the evidence comes from a cross-sectional design, these correlations support construct validity at a single assessment but cannot establish the EQ-5D's responsiveness or sensitivity to change over time in acute coronary syndrome patients.

In 40 healthy eyes, two examiners took three repeated measurements with each instrument; mean pupil diameter was 5.81 ± 0.70 mm with SLBM versus 6.26 ± 0.68 mm with Colvard infrared pupillometry (CIP) when averaging both examiners' results (p = 0.01).
Mean differences between SLBM and CIP were -0.60 mm and -0.30 mm for the two examiners using the average of three readings (p = 0.02), and were very similar using the first reading.
Intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.97 and 0.92 for SLBM, compared with 0.96 and 0.90 for CIP.
For detection of pupils larger than 6 mm, SLBM sensitivity ranged from 55.56% to 73.68% and specificity from 76.19% to 95.45%.

Analysis of two nationally representative cross-sectional household surveys conducted in Kenya in 2003 and 2007, covering the public, private-not-for-profit and private-for-profit sectors, found that all three sectors recorded similar levels of pro-rich distribution in 2003, but by 2007 the private-not-for-profit sector was pro-poor, public sector benefits showed an equal distribution, and the private-for-profit sector remained pro-rich; larger pro-rich disparities were recorded for inpatient compared with outpatient benefits at the hospital level, while primary health care services were pro-poor.

Universal coverage involves ensuring that health care benefits are distributed on the basis of need for care and not on ability to pay; in the Kenyan health system assessed in this study, benefits were distributed on the basis of ability to pay and not on need for care, indicating that the distribution did not meet the principles of universal coverage.

In young obese males, mean common carotid artery pulsatility index and resistance index were statistically higher than in healthy controls; these indexes were calculated from blood flow velocity curves obtained by pulsed Doppler ultrasonography in 35 young obese males and 23 age-matched healthy male volunteers.

Yes — in an in vivo animal study, serum levels of lidocaine and its metabolite monoethylglycinexylidide (MEGX) were undetectable in untreated skin, whereas following laser treatment both lidocaine and MEGX were detectable, indicating that laser pretreatment enhanced transdermal absorption of topical lidocaine.
The aim of this study was to demonstrate in vivo firstly that laser enhances transdermal drug absorption and secondly that this can be manipulated by altering laser settings.
Four pigs were used in the IACUC approved animal study.
On day 0, 5 g of 4% topical lidocaine was applied under occlusion for 60 minutes to a 400 cm(2) area on the abdomen.
On day 7, the Er:YAG laser was used at 500, 250, 50, and 25 µm ablative depth, respectively, over a 400 cm(2) area on the abdomen.
Five grams of 4% topical lidocaine was applied immediately with occlusion for 60 minutes, and then removed.
Blood was drawn at 0, 60, 90, 120, 180, and 240 minutes.
The serum was extracted and analyzed for lidocaine and its metabolite monoethylglycinexylidide (MEGX).
Peak levels of lidocaine were significantly higher (P = 0.0002) at 250 µm (0.62 mg/L), compared to 500 µm (0.45 mg/L), 50 µm (0.48 mg/L), and 25 µm (0.3 mg/L).
Peak levels of MEGX were significantly higher (P ≤ 0.0001) at 250 µm (0.048 mg/L), compared to 500 µm (0.018 mg/L), 50 µm (0.036 mg/L), and 25 µm (0.0144 mg/L).

Because these findings come from an animal model, they establish enhanced transdermal absorption of topical lidocaine under the experimental conditions tested rather than a demonstrated clinical benefit in patients.

Ultrasound retains a role in the assessment of internal derangements of the temporomandibular joint, but with acknowledged limitations: imaging by static and dynamic high-resolution ultrasound demonstrated considerably lower sensitivity compared with magnetic resonance, and the presence of articular sounds and physical signs was often insufficient to detect disk displacement.

In this diagnostic study, 40 patients and 20 asymptomatic volunteers (120 temporomandibular joints) underwent a standardized interview, physical examination, and static and dynamic articular ultrasound, with sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values calculated against magnetic resonance as the reference test.
The authors reported that some of the technical difficulties of the ultrasound examination resulted from limited access because of the presence of surrounding bone structures.

Ioflupane, N-u-fluoropropyl-2a-carbomethoxy-3a-(4-iodophenyl) nortropane, also called FP-CIT, labelled with (123)I (commercially known as DaTSCAN) has been proven to be useful in the differential diagnosis between PD and ET and to confirm dopaminergic degeneration in patients with parkinsonism. the authors used DaTSCAN to obtain SPECT images and measure the radiopharmaceutical uptake in the striatum (S), as well as the caudate nucleus (CN) and putamen (P) in all individuals.

In addition, 33 patients (11 males and 22 females) with an established diagnosis of PD with unilateral limb involvement (12 left hemi-body and 21 right hemi-body) were included for comparison with ET.
Semiquantitative analysis revealed significant differences between NV and ET patients in the striatum, reduced in the latter.

In this study DaTSCAN SPECT separated PD from ET: reduced accumulation of the radiopharmaceutical uptake was found in the putamen of all PD patients, there was a significant reduction in tracer accumulation in the left putamen of patients with right hemi-parkinsonism compared with ET and NV, and patients with left hemi-parkinsonism showed reduced radioligand uptake in the right putamen in comparison with ET and NV.

Clinical follow-up of 20 patients with ET (interval not specified in the source) revealed no significant change in clinical presentation, particularly no signs of PD, and follow-up DaTSCAN performed in 10 of them was negative in all but one, that single patient having had an equivocal baseline study which deteriorated 12 months later.

Resection of SLM and CRC can be undertaken at different centres (separate management, SM) or at the same centre (global management, GM); a retrospective study of SLM and CRC resections carried out during 01/2000 - 12/2006 by SM or GM, using a combined or delayed strategy, compared these approaches.

Among patients whose liver resection was delayed (62 SM, 17 GM), chemotherapy before liver surgery was given to 92% of SM versus 38% of GM patients (P<0.0001), and the median delay between the two procedures was 212 days for SM versus 182 days for GM (P = 0.04); the first step of liver resection was performed during colorectal surgery in 62% of GM versus 6% of SM patients (P<0.0001), and the mean number of procedures (CRC+SLM) was lower in GM at 1.6 versus 2.3 in SM (P = 0.003).
Three-month mortality was 3% in the GM group and 0% in the SM group, a difference that was not statistically significant.
Overall survival was 67% for SM versus 51% for GM at 3 years and 35% versus 31% at 5 years, with neither comparison statistically significant.

Yes — in the 1993 Pelotas birth cohort, obesity at the start of adolescence was a risk factor for wheezing: the prevalence of wheezing at 15 years was 50% greater among individuals who were obese at 11 years than among those who were eutrophic at 11 years (RR 1.53; 95% CI: 1.14-2.05), independent of the effect of various confounding variables.
After controlling for confounding factors, the risk of persistent wheezing among individuals who were obese at 11 years was 1.82 (95% CI: 1.30-2.54).
The greater the skinfold tertile at 11 years, the higher the prevalence of wheezing at 15 years was (p =.011).
Weight status and skinfolds did not present any association with incident wheezing.

A training model for retroperitoneoscopic nephrectomy (RPN) exists and was developed experimentally in a porcine (piglet) model, in which fifteen piglets were operated on and fifteen RPNs were performed, all with three ports.
The authors report that RPN in a porcine model could simulate the whole procedure, from creating the retroperitoneal space to nephrectomy completion.

After statistical data analysis, the experimental learning curve for the porcine RPN training model was eight cases; animals were divided into group A (the first eight cases) and group B (the last seven cases), with statistically significant differences between the groups in peritoneal opening (p = 0.025), operative time (p = 0.0037) and blood loss (p = 0.026).

In these fifteen porcine RPNs, operative time ranged from 15 to 50 minutes (median 30 minutes) and blood loss ranged from 5 to 100 mL (median 20 mL), with five peritoneal openings and two surgical vascular complications managed laparoscopically.
The evidence for this model comes from an experimental animal (piglet) study, so it supports the feasibility of a training model rather than clinical outcomes in patients.

The retrieved evidence is insufficient to establish whether etoricoxib prevents heterotopic ossification after primary total hip arthroplasty relative to placebo or another NSAID, because the only identified study was a single-arm prospective two-stage phase-2 design in a small sample (n = 42) that reported outcomes only for patients who took etoricoxib.

In that study, oral etoricoxib 90 mg was given for seven days to patients who received a cemented primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis, and heterotopic ossification was determined six months after surgery on anteroposterior pelvic radiographs using the Brooker classification.
Among the patients who took etoricoxib, no heterotopic ossification was found in 62%, while 31% had Brooker grade 1 and 7% had Brooker grade 2 ossification.

For articles published in the intensive care medicine journal Intensive Care Medicine in 2008, the retrieved evidence on whether open access publishing increases impact is mixed: the median number of citations was 8 (interquartile range 4-12) for non-open access articles versus 9 (6-18) for open access articles, a difference that was not statistically significant (p=0.084).
Among the most-cited articles (citation range >8), the citation count was 13 (10-16) for non-open access articles and 18 (13-21) for open access articles (p=0.008).
In the 30-35 months after publication, the average number of citations per article per month was 0.28 ± 0.6 for non-open access articles versus 0.38 ± 0.7 for open access articles (p=0.043).

In a linear multiple regression model adjusting for potentially confounding variables, independent factors for citation advantage were the Hirsch index of the first signing author (β=0.207; p=0.015) and open access status (β=3.618; p=0.006).
The analysis evaluated 161 articles, 76% of which were non-open access, published in Intensive Care Medicine in 2008, with citation data compared between the two groups up until April 30, 2011.

Because this evidence comes from a single discipline — intensive care medicine — and from one journal's 2008 output, it cannot establish that open access publishing increases the impact of scientific articles generally, and the relationship between open access and citation counts in intensive care medicine had not been studied previously.

In a canine model, a solitary kidney was more resistant to warm ischemia than paired kidneys: after 90 minutes of left renal artery occlusion, group 1 (solitary kidney created by right nephrectomy, 10 dogs) showed a smaller fall in clearance and less tubular necrosis than group 2 (10 dogs with both kidneys).

In group 1 (solitary kidney) clearance decreased by 20% at 1 week and basal function was regained starting at week 2, whereas in group 2 (both kidneys) clearance decreased by more than 90% up to week 2, recovery started only at week 3, and by 4 weeks a 23% clearance reduction persisted.

Histopathology showed significant tubular necrosis (60%) at 3 days in group 1 with regeneration starting at 1 week, versus more pronounced tubular necrosis (90%) in group 2 with regeneration starting at 2 weeks.

Expression of the proinflammatory markers CD95 and tumor necrosis factor-α, assessed by real-time polymerase chain reaction, was up-regulated in each group, with higher and more sustained expression in group 2 (both kidneys) than in group 1 (solitary kidney).

The authors state that to their knowledge there were no evidence-based medicine data to date to critically judge the vulnerability of a solitary kidney to warm ischemia compared with paired kidneys, and the comparison reported here derives from a dog model in which right nephrectomy created the solitary kidney, so it does not by itself establish the same differential response in humans.
